<div class="page-heading story-heading">
  <p class="eyebrow">A measured question, not a simple answer</p>
  <h1>When Emotions Become Physical</h1>
  <p>What does a self-reported symptom scale have to do with a blood marker? This comparison offers a careful starting point.</p>
</div>

```{r}
source("scripts/prepare_data.R")
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
data <- read_clean_data()
severity_levels <- c("Minimal", "Mild", "Moderate", "Moderately severe", "Severe")
severity_summary <- data |>
  dplyr::mutate(phq9_category = factor(phq9_category, levels = severity_levels)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(phq9_category, .drop = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    elevated_n = sum(elevated_hscrp),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    elevated_pct = ifelse(n > 0, 100 * elevated_n / n, NA_real_),
    denominator = paste0("n = ", format(n, big.mark = ","))
  )
severity_present <- dplyr::filter(severity_summary, n > 0)
```

## The share above 3 mg/L

Each bar is the percentage of participants in that PHQ-9 symptom group whose hs-CRP was above 3 mg/L. Denominators are shown below the group labels; values describe this complete-case sample, not the U.S. population.

```{r}
ggplot(severity_present, aes(x = phq9_category, y = elevated_pct)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.66, fill = "#78A98B", color = "#244A3C", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", elevated_pct)),
    vjust = -0.65,
    color = "#244A3C",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(y = -4.7, label = denominator),
    color = "#53695c",
    size = 3.2
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = TRUE, labels = function(x) gsub(" ", "\n", x, fixed = TRUE)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-7, max(severity_present$elevated_pct, na.rm = TRUE) + 10),
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "PHQ-9 depressive symptom group",
    y = "Participants with hs-CRP > 3 mg/L",
    caption = paste0(
      "Unweighted complete-case percentages · N = ", format(nrow(data), big.mark = ","),
      " · hs-CRP threshold: >3 mg/L."
    )
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#e1e9e3"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(color = "#294a3d", lineheight = 0.96, margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#294a3d"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#5b7163", hjust = 0),
    plot.margin = margin(16, 20, 42, 12)
  )
```

The question here is whether the proportion above a commonly used hs-CRP threshold differs across PHQ-9 symptom groups in adults who completed all the selected NHANES measures. The PHQ-9 asks about nine symptoms over the previous two weeks; it is a screening measure, not a diagnosis or a complete account of someone's emotional life.

In this sample, the observed proportions range from **`r sprintf("%.1f%%", min(severity_present$elevated_pct))`** to **`r sprintf("%.1f%%", max(severity_present$elevated_pct))`** across groups. The group denominators shown on the chart matter: the more severe symptom categories can have fewer participants, so their percentages may be less stable. These figures are unweighted descriptions, not adjusted estimates for all U.S. adults.

A 2026 NHANES analysis by Arellano and colleagues examined hs-CRP and depression symptom severity using multivariable methods. That peer-reviewed work provides context, but this project uses a complete-case subset and does not apply survey weights or reproduce its adjusted analyses. A separate 2024 cross-sectional study also examines hs-CRP alongside depressive symptoms.

NHANES is observational and these measurements do not establish which came first, explain an association, or rule out other factors. hs-CRP is a nonspecific marker of inflammation—not a measure of immune strength, emotional experience as a whole, or how quickly a person recovers.

<div class="editorial-callout editorial-callout-note"><span class="callout-icon" aria-hidden="true">i</span><div><strong>Interpret with care</strong><p>Group-level percentages cannot diagnose individuals. This visualization does not measure immune function or healing speed, and it does not support a cause-and-effect conclusion.</p></div></div>
